stem.en: To measure the current in a circuit, an ammeter is connected:

options.en: Either in series or in parallel

explanation.en: The whole current to be measured must pass through the ammeter, so it goes in series. Its resistance must be very small so that it does not change the current.

stem.en: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting:

options.en: A high resistance in parallel with it
A high resistance in series with it
A low resistance in series with it
A low resistance (shunt) in parallel with it

explanation.en: The shunt carries most of the current, so only the safe full-scale current I_g passes through the coil. The combination also has a very low resistance, as an ammeter should.

stem.en: A permanent magnet moving coil (PMMC) instrument, used on its own, can measure:

explanation.en: The deflecting torque depends on the direction of the current, so on a.c. the pointer would just vibrate about zero. PMMC meters measure d.c.; with a rectifier they can read a.c. Their scale is linear.

stem.en: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full-scale deflection for 1 mA. The shunt needed to make it an ammeter of range 0–1 A is about:
The same galvanometer (G = 100 Ω, I_g = 1 mA) is to be made a voltmeter of range 0–10 V. The series resistance needed is:
On the scale of a series-type ohmmeter, zero ohms is marked at:

explanation.en: With the leads shorted (R_x = 0) the maximum current flows and the pointer goes to full scale, so 0 Ω is at the right end and ∞ is at the left end.

stem.en: Before measuring a resistance with an analog ohmmeter, you should:

options.en: Leave the leads open and set the pointer to zero
Short the test leads and set the pointer to zero ohms with the zero-adjust control
Connect the meter to the circuit supply

explanation.en: Shorting the leads and adjusting the zero-adjust (variable) resistor compensates for the ageing of the internal cell. Never measure resistance in a live circuit.

stem.en: The resistance scale of an analog multimeter is:

options.en: Linear, with zero on the left
The same as the voltage scale
Non-linear and reversed (zero on the right)

explanation.en: The current is I = E/(R_h + R_x), which is not proportional to R_x, so the scale is crowded towards the high-resistance (left) end and runs from right to left.

stem.en: A series ohmmeter has a total internal resistance (half-scale value) of 4.5 kΩ. An unknown resistance that gives exactly half-scale deflection is:

explanation.en: I = E/(R_h + R_x). Half of full-scale current E/R_h flows when R_x = R_h = 4.5 kΩ. That is why R_h is called the half-scale resistance.

solution.en: Half of full-scale current E/R_h flows when R_x = R_h = 4.5 kΩ.
That is why R_h is called the half-scale resistance.

stem.en: A series ohmmeter has an internal (half-scale) resistance of 5 kΩ. When a 15 kΩ resistor is connected, the pointer deflects to what fraction of full scale?

explanation.en: Fraction = R_h/(R_h + R_x) = 5/(5 + 15) = 0.25, one quarter of full scale.

stem.en: The block of a digital multimeter that converts the measured analog voltage into a digital number is the:

explanation.en: Every quantity is first converted to a d.c. voltage; the ADC turns this voltage into a count, which is decoded and shown on the display.

stem.en: The largest number a 3½-digit display can show is:

explanation.en: A 3½-digit display has three full digits (0–9) and a leading "half digit" that can only be 0 or 1, so it reads up to 1999.

stem.en: An important advantage of a digital multimeter over an analog multimeter is:

options.en: Its high input impedance (about 10 MΩ), which loads the circuit very little
It does not need an ADC

explanation.en: A DMM has a high, constant input impedance on all voltage ranges, gives a direct numerical reading with no parallax error, and often has auto-ranging and polarity indication.

stem.en: The resolution of a 3½-digit DMM on its 2 V range (maximum reading 1.999 V) is:

explanation.en: The smallest change shown is one count in the last digit: 0.001 V = 1 mV.

solution.en: The smallest change shown is one count in the last digit: 0.001 V = 1 mV.

stem.en: A 3½-digit DMM on its 2 V range has an accuracy of ±(0.5 % of reading + 2 counts). For a reading of 1.500 V, the possible error is:

explanation.en: 0.5 % of 1.500 V = 7.5 mV; 2 counts × 1 mV = 2 mV; total ±9.5 mV. (±12 mV wrongly takes 0.5 % of the full range.)

stem.en: The part of a cathode ray tube that produces a fine, focused beam of electrons is the:

explanation.en: The electron gun has a heated cathode, a control grid, and focusing and accelerating anodes that produce a narrow, fast electron beam.

stem.en: The time-base (sweep) voltage applied to the horizontal deflection plates of a CRO has the shape of a:

explanation.en: A sawtooth rises linearly, moving the spot across the screen at constant speed, then drops quickly (flyback) to start the next sweep.

stem.en: In a CRO, the signal to be displayed is applied (through the vertical amplifier) to the:

explanation.en: The signal moves the spot up and down through the Y plates, while the time base sweeps it across through the X plates, tracing the waveform against time.

stem.en: The aquadag (graphite) coating on the inside of a cathode ray tube:

options.en: Gives out the light seen on the screen
Collects the secondary electrons knocked out of the screen

explanation.en: When the beam hits the phosphor, secondary electrons are emitted. The conducting aquadag coating, connected to the accelerating anode, collects them so that the screen does not charge up.

solution.en: When the beam hits the phosphor, secondary electrons are emitted.
The conducting aquadag coating, connected to the accelerating anode, collects them so that the screen does not charge up.

stem.en: In a CRT, the deflection plates are 2 cm long and 0.5 cm apart, the screen is 20 cm from the plates and the accelerating voltage is 1000 V. Using D = L l V_d/(2 d V_a), a deflecting voltage of 50 V moves the spot by:
A sine wave on a CRO screen is 6 divisions high from peak to peak, with the vertical control at 2 V/div. Its peak-to-peak voltage is:

explanation.en: V_pp = divisions × volts/div = 6 × 2 = 12 V (so V_m = 6 V).

stem.en: One full cycle of a waveform spans 4 divisions with the time base at 5 ms/div. Its frequency is:
Two sine signals of equal amplitude and equal frequency are applied to the X and Y plates. The Lissajous figure is a circle when the phase difference is:

explanation.en: 0° gives a straight line at 45°, 180° a line the other way, 45° an ellipse, and 90° (with equal amplitudes) a circle.

stem.en: A Lissajous figure touches a horizontal tangent line at 2 points and a vertical tangent line at 1 point. If the frequency on the X plates is 1 kHz, the frequency on the Y plates is:

explanation.en: f_y/f_x = (number of horizontal tangencies)/(number of vertical tangencies) = 2/1, so f_y = 2 × 1 kHz = 2 kHz.

solution.en: f_y/f_x = (number of horizontal tangencies)/(number of vertical tangencies) = 2/1, so f_y = 2 × 1 kHz = 2 kHz.

stem.en: A sine wave measures 8 divisions peak to peak at 0.5 V/div. Its r.m.s. value is about:
The sensitivity of a voltmeter built from a 50 µA full-scale movement is:

explanation.en: Sensitivity = 1/I_fsd = 1/(50 × 10⁻⁶ A) = 20 000 Ω/V. A higher Ω/V rating loads the circuit less.

solution.en: A higher Ω/V rating loads the circuit less.

stem.en: For an electrostatically deflected CRT, the deflection of the spot on the screen is:

options.en: Directly proportional to the deflecting voltage
Directly proportional to the accelerating voltage
Proportional to the square of the deflecting voltage

explanation.en: D = L l V_d/(2 d V_a): it is proportional to V_d and inversely proportional to the accelerating voltage V_a. This linearity lets the CRO measure voltages.

solution.en: D = L l V_d/(2 d V_a): it is proportional to V_d and inversely proportional to the accelerating voltage V_a.
This linearity lets the CRO measure voltages.

stem.en: Two signals of the same frequency give an ellipse on a CRO. The ellipse cuts the Y axis at ±3 divisions and its maximum height is ±6 divisions. The phase difference between the signals is:

explanation.en: sin φ = (Y-intercept)/(maximum Y) = 3/6 = 0.5, so φ = 30°.

stem.en: Thermionic emission from a heated filament in vacuum was first noticed as the:

explanation.en: Edison saw current flow from a hot filament to a separate plate in 1883. Fleming used it to build the vacuum diode in 1904.

stem.en: A step-up transformer is an active component because its output voltage is larger than its input voltage.

explanation.en: It raises voltage but lowers current. Output power is never more than input power, so there is no power gain. It is passive.

stem.en: Why are digital signals preferred for storing and sending information?

explanation.en: Small noise added to a digital signal does not change whether it is read as 0 or 1, so the information survives.

options.en: They can take every value in a range
They are less affected by noise, since only HIGH and LOW must be told apart

stem.en: The output of a microphone is best described as:

explanation.en: The microphone voltage follows the sound wave smoothly, so it is analog. It becomes digital only after an ADC.

stem.en: The internal resistance of an ideal current source is:

explanation.en: With infinite parallel resistance, none of the source current is diverted away from the load.

stem.en: The terminal voltage of a practical battery rises when it supplies more current.

explanation.en: V = E − Ir, so a larger I means more lost volts and a smaller terminal voltage.

stem.en: How many electrons make up a charge of 1 C?
The first commercial microprocessor was:

explanation.en: The 4-bit Intel 4004 came out in 1971. The 8085 and 8086 came later in the 1970s.

stem.en: A diode is listed among active devices in board textbooks.

explanation.en: Diodes are semiconductor devices that control the direction of current, so board books group them with active devices.
